formula: score ~ treatment + gender + phase + hour + (1 | id)
notes: Contrived repeated-measures data (O'Brien & Kaiser 1985, Psych. Bulletin 97), long form of OBrienKaiser; 16 subjects (id) measured across the within-subject factors phase (pre/post/fup) and hour (1-5), with treatment and gender between-subjects. The page describes the design (two between- and two within-subject factors) but gives no model formula; rendered as a subject random-intercept with the four factors as main effects. Full between x within factorial (treatment*gender*phase*hour) noted but not expanded into the interactions column.

Soil composition in a randomized block design: 4 blocks, 3 contours x 4 depths (Horton et al. 1968; Friendly 2006 JSS 17(6); Khattree & Naik 2000). The page states a two-way randomized block design and lists 9 response variables (MANOVA/canonical discriminant). Census blocked-design rule applied: fixed RBD rendered as the random-intercept version on Block at low confidence. RULE GAP: MANOVA with multiple continuous responses (pH, N, Dens, P, Ca, Mg, K, Na, Conduc); filed pH as the single response and the other eight in ignore; derived group encodings Group and Gp also in ignore. Depth is quantitative/ordered on the page but not stored as an R ordered factor, so no types declared.

Chemical composition of ancient pottery from 4 British sites (Hand et al. 1994, A Handbook of Small Data Sets), used to illustrate MANOVA in the SAS manual. Multiple pottery samples repeat within Site (an explicit grouping example). Census fixed-design-to-random rule applied: one-way layout rendered as a random intercept on Site at low confidence. RULE GAP: MANOVA with 5 chemical responses (Al, Fe, Mg, Ca, Na) and Site as the discriminating fixed factor of interest; filed Al as the single response, the other four chemicals in ignore; no covariates.

formula: piq ~ days + duration + sex + age + (1 | id)
notes: Longitudinal post-coma IQ recovery for 200 patients with traumatic brain injury (Wong, Monette & Weiner 2001, Brain Injury 15), 331 measurements (avg 1.7 per patient). Grouping factor id (subject); days = time post-coma (the longitudinal axis), duration = coma length, with sex and age. The page describes the longitudinal design but gives no explicit formula; rendered as a subject random-intercept. piq (performance IQ) filed as response; viq (verbal IQ, a parallel alternate response) in ignore.
